title: Inverse image of the extension by the empty set of a constant sheaf on an open subset
statement: Let $g:Z'\to Z$ be a continuous map of topological spaces, $V\subseteq Z$ an open subset, $V'=g^{-1}(V)$ and $T$ a set. For an open $W$ of a space and a set $T$ let $j_{W!}\underline T$ be the extension by the empty set of the sheaf $\underline T_W$ of locally constant maps to $T$ on $W$, with sheafification map $\theta:j_{W,p!}\underline T_W\to j_{W!}\underline T$ [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty]; for $t\in T$ let $\mathrm{const}_t\in\underline T_W(W)=(j_{W,p!}\underline T_W)(W)$ be the constant map, and for a sheaf of sets $\mathcal K$ on the space let $\beta_{\mathcal K}:\operatorname{Hom}(j_{W!}\underline T,\mathcal K)\to\operatorname{Map}(T,\mathcal K(W))$, $\psi\mapsto(t\mapsto\psi_W(\theta_W(\mathrm{const}_t)))$ (a bijection). Let $g^{-1}$ be the inverse image of sheaves of sets with unit $\eta^g_{\mathcal K,W}:\mathcal K(W)\to(g^{-1}\mathcal K)(g^{-1}W)$ on sections, as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets. Then there is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets $\lambda:g^{-1}(j_{V!}\underline T)\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{V'!}\underline T$ on $Z'$ such that for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal K$ on $Z$ and every morphism $\psi:j_{V!}\underline T\to\mathcal K$ one has $\beta_{g^{-1}\mathcal K}(g^{-1}\psi\circ\lambda^{-1})=\eta^g_{\mathcal K,V}\circ\beta_{\mathcal K}(\psi)$ as maps $T\to(g^{-1}\mathcal K)(V')$ (with $\beta$ taken for $W=V'$ on the left and $W=V$ on the right).

proof.text: *Step 1 ($\beta$ is a bijection, natural in $\mathcal K$).* Let $X$ be one of the spaces $Z$, $Z'$, $W\subseteq X$ open, $T$ a set and $\mathcal K$ a sheaf of sets on $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty-adjunction] (2), applied to $U=W$ and $\mathcal G=\underline T_W$, the map $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta)|_W$, $\operatorname{Hom}(j_{W!}\underline T,\mathcal K)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\underline T_W,\mathcal K|_W)$, is bijective, where $\mathcal K|_W$ is a sheaf of sets on $W$ (the statement of that node). By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-open-maps-sections], applied to the space $W$, the set $T$ and the sheaf $\mathcal K|_W$, the map $\varphi\mapsto(t\mapsto\varphi_W(\mathrm{const}_t))$, $\operatorname{Hom}(\underline T_W,\mathcal K|_W)\to\operatorname{Map}(T,\mathcal K|_W(W))=\operatorname{Map}(T,\mathcal K(W))$, is bijective. The composite sends $\psi$ to $t\mapsto((\psi\circ\theta)|_W)_W(\mathrm{const}_t)=\psi_W(\theta_W(\mathrm{const}_t))$, where $\mathrm{const}_t\in\underline T_W(W)=(j_{W,p!}\underline T_W)(W)$ [def-weil-pbc-sets-extension-by-empty]; this is $\beta_{\mathcal K}(\psi)$. So $\beta_{\mathcal K}$ is bijective. Naturality: for a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K'$ of sheaves of sets on $X$, $(\alpha\circ\psi)_W=\alpha_W\circ\psi_W$, hence $\beta_{\mathcal K'}(\alpha\circ\psi)=\alpha_W\circ\beta_{\mathcal K}(\psi)$ $(\ast)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00A3 (label lemma-j-shriek, line 4549) for the adjunction of j_{W!} with restriction; maps out of the sheaf of locally constant maps: Example Tag 0081 (label example-sheafify-constant) and literature/stacks-project/sites.tex Example Tag 0H7J (label example-constant-sheaf); as used in literature/stacks-project/modules.tex Lemma Tag 0CAH (label lemma-surjection) and the proof of Lemma Tag 0CAK ('correspond by adjunction to two families ... of maps of sets')

proof.text: *Step 2 (the adjunction $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ in the form used).* For a sheaf of sets $\mathcal K$ on $Z'$, $g_*\mathcal K$ is the sheaf of sets $W\mapsto\mathcal K(g^{-1}W)$ on $Z$, and $(g_*k)_W=k_{g^{-1}W}$ for a morphism $k$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (1) (with values in sets); in particular $(g_*\mathcal K)(V)=\mathcal K(V')$ and $(g_*k)_V=k_{V'}$. For a sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $Z$ let $\eta^g_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to g_*g^{-1}\mathcal G$, $\eta^g_{\mathcal G,W}=\theta_{\mathcal G,g^{-1}W}\circ\iota^{g^{-1}W}_W$, be the unit of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3). By the adjunction $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ for sheaves of sets [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-colimits-finite-products] (a), with this unit as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (3) (the composite bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(g^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal K)=\operatorname{Hom}(g_p\mathcal G,\mathcal K)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,g_*\mathcal K)$ there sends $\varphi$ to $g_*(\varphi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G})\circ i_{\mathcal G}=g_*\varphi\circ\eta^g_{\mathcal G}$), the map $a_{\mathcal G,\mathcal K}:\operatorname{Hom}(g^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal K)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,g_*\mathcal K)$, $\varphi\mapsto g_*\varphi\circ\eta^g_{\mathcal G}$, is bijective. It is natural in $\mathcal K$: $a(k\circ\varphi)=g_*k\circ g_*\varphi\circ\eta^g_{\mathcal G}=g_*k\circ a(\varphi)$ for $k:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K'$. The unit is natural: for a morphism $\psi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ of sheaves of sets on $Z$, $g_*(g^{-1}\psi)\circ\eta^g_{\mathcal G}=\eta^g_{\mathcal H}\circ\psi$ $(\ast\ast)$; on sections over $W$ this reads $(g^{-1}\psi)_{g^{-1}W}\circ\theta_{\mathcal G,g^{-1}W}\circ\iota^{g^{-1}W}_W=\theta_{\mathcal H,g^{-1}W}\circ(g_p\psi)_{g^{-1}W}\circ\iota^{g^{-1}W}_W=\theta_{\mathcal H,g^{-1}W}\circ\iota^{g^{-1}W}_W\circ\psi_W$, by the defining equations $g^{-1}\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}=\theta_{\mathcal H}\circ g_p\psi$ and $(g_p\psi)_U\circ\iota^U_W=\iota^U_W\circ\psi_W$ of [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3).

source.place: Lemma Tag 008K (label lemma-f-map, line 2249): bijection between maps G -> f_*F and maps f^{-1}G -> F, functorially in F and G

proof.text: *Step 3 (both sheaves corepresent the same functor).* Put $\mathcal A=g^{-1}(j_{V!}\underline T)$ and $\mathcal B=j_{V'!}\underline T$, sheaves of sets on $Z'$ ($V'=g^{-1}(V)$ is open since $g$ is continuous). Write $\beta^V$ for $\beta$ with $W=V$ on $Z$ and $\beta^{V'}$ for $\beta$ with $W=V'$ on $Z'$. For every sheaf of sets $\mathcal K$ on $Z'$ define $\Phi_{\mathcal K}:\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal A,\mathcal K)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal B,\mathcal K)$ by $\Phi_{\mathcal K}=(\beta^{V'}_{\mathcal K})^{-1}\circ\beta^V_{g_*\mathcal K}\circ a_{j_{V!}\underline T,\mathcal K}$; this makes sense since $\beta^V_{g_*\mathcal K}$ takes values in $\operatorname{Map}(T,(g_*\mathcal K)(V))=\operatorname{Map}(T,\mathcal K(V'))$ (Step 2), the target of $\beta^{V'}_{\mathcal K}$. It is a composite of bijections (Steps 1, 2), so bijective. Naturality in $\mathcal K$: for $k:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K'$ and $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal K$, by Step 2 and $(\ast)$ for $g_*k$ on $Z$, $\beta^V_{g_*\mathcal K'}(a(k\circ\varphi))=\beta^V_{g_*\mathcal K'}(g_*k\circ a(\varphi))=(g_*k)_V\circ\beta^V_{g_*\mathcal K}(a(\varphi))=k_{V'}\circ\beta^{V'}_{\mathcal K}(\Phi_{\mathcal K}(\varphi))$, and by $(\ast)$ for $k$ on $Z'$ the last map is $\beta^{V'}_{\mathcal K'}(k\circ\Phi_{\mathcal K}(\varphi))$. Applying $(\beta^{V'}_{\mathcal K'})^{-1}$: $\Phi_{\mathcal K'}(k\circ\varphi)=k\circ\Phi_{\mathcal K}(\varphi)$. (In words: $\operatorname{Hom}(g^{-1}j_{V!}\underline T,\mathcal K)=\operatorname{Hom}(j_{V!}\underline T,g_*\mathcal K)=\operatorname{Map}(T,\mathcal K(V'))=\operatorname{Hom}(j_{V'!}\underline T,\mathcal K)$, naturally in $\mathcal K$.)

proof.text: *Step 4 (Yoneda: the isomorphism $\lambda$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] in the category of sheaves of sets on $Z'$, applied to the objects $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ and the bijections $\Phi_{\mathcal K}$, natural in $\mathcal K$ (Step 3), the morphism $\vartheta=\Phi_{\mathcal A}(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}):\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ is an isomorphism and $\Phi_{\mathcal K}(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\vartheta$ for every $\mathcal K$ and every $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal K$. Put $\lambda=\vartheta^{-1}:g^{-1}(j_{V!}\underline T)\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{V'!}\underline T$, an isomorphism of sheaves of sets on $Z'$, with $\lambda^{-1}=\vartheta$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 001P (label lemma-yoneda), in the opposite category

proof.text: *Step 5 (compatibility with $\beta$ and $\eta^g$).* Let $\mathcal K$ be a sheaf of sets on $Z$ and $\psi:j_{V!}\underline T\to\mathcal K$. Then $g^{-1}\psi:\mathcal A\to g^{-1}\mathcal K$, and by Step 4 $g^{-1}\psi\circ\lambda^{-1}=g^{-1}\psi\circ\vartheta=\Phi_{g^{-1}\mathcal K}(g^{-1}\psi)$. By the definition of $\Phi$ (Step 3), $\beta^{V'}_{g^{-1}\mathcal K}(g^{-1}\psi\circ\lambda^{-1})=\beta^V_{g_*g^{-1}\mathcal K}(a(g^{-1}\psi))=\beta^V_{g_*g^{-1}\mathcal K}(g_*(g^{-1}\psi)\circ\eta^g_{j_{V!}\underline T})$. By $(\ast\ast)$ of Step 2 (with $\mathcal G=j_{V!}\underline T$, $\mathcal H=\mathcal K$) this is $\beta^V_{g_*g^{-1}\mathcal K}(\eta^g_{\mathcal K}\circ\psi)$, and by $(\ast)$ of Step 1 for $\alpha=\eta^g_{\mathcal K}:\mathcal K\to g_*g^{-1}\mathcal K$ on $Z$ it equals $(\eta^g_{\mathcal K})_V\circ\beta^V_{\mathcal K}(\psi)=\eta^g_{\mathcal K,V}\circ\beta_{\mathcal K}(\psi)$, as maps $T\to(g_*g^{-1}\mathcal K)(V)=(g^{-1}\mathcal K)(V')$. This is the asserted identity.
